notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Super Mario 64 and Star Fox 64 join Ports and Apps as native versions by HarbourMasters: Ghostship and Starship. Each plays from your own US cartridge ROM (Star Fox 64 1.0 or 1.1): add it on the web page and the first launch prepares the game once, in about 20 seconds for Mario and about 80 for Star Fox. Frame rate in the game's Performance settings picks 30 (the original) or 60 (smoother). Mods go in on the web page as .o2r files. A Ghostship mod can carry code that runs on the console, so install only mods you trust.

Super Mario 64, Star Fox 64 and Mario Kart 64 also take .n64 and .v64 ROM files now.

Sleep in a game: a press of the power button in a game now puts the console into deep sleep too, not just the screen-off pause. The game's state is saved, the game is paused and muted, and when you wake the console it carries on with its own clock profile. Before, a console left in a game kept its controllers lit and was flat by morning.

Jak and Daxter, Jak II, Jak 3, Sly Cooper, Wind Waker HD and The Wind Waker now take the controller in port 1, instead of whichever one the game found first: attached Joy-Cons no longer take over from a Pro Controller. Wind Waker HD rumbles only that controller.

Controller setup reads a trigger as analog on pads that report it both ways, like DualShock-style pads and the GameSir G8+, so Moonlight gets the full trigger range. Run controller setup again for such a pad.

The RAM and CPU tuners can test with the save state you pick: a Test game row on Run a Tuning Session, Set a Custom RAM Setting and the CPU undervolt's Run Tuner. Automatic still uses your largest GameCube or Wii game with a save state.

Not tried yet: a real overnight sleep in a game (the wake was tested with a stand-in for the suspend), the controller order with a Pro Controller and attached Joy-Cons, and the trigger fix on a real DualShock-style pad. Reports welcome.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
